key_insight: LLM agents derived a shared clinical data schema from 24,588 sarcoma case report abstracts, consolidating 72,909 candidate data elements into 1,570. Of these, 53 met a support threshold of at least 50 abstracts and were selected for evidence-linked extraction.
problem_solved: Common data elements make clinical reports easier to compare, but defining them manually is labor-intensive. This study explores automating both schema discovery and structured information extraction from unstructured medical abstracts.
method: Use an LLM agent to propose candidate common data elements from 24,588 PubMed abstracts.
Consolidate 72,909 candidates into 1,570 elements, then retain 53 supported by at least 50 abstracts each.
Attempt evidence-linked extraction for the retained elements across the corpus.
impact: The approach suggests a scalable path from clinical text to structured, source-linked data. The supplied abstract is truncated, so extraction accuracy and complete processing outcomes cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Funnel: 72,909 candidates → 1,570 consolidated elements → 53 retained elements.
Workflow diagram: PubMed abstracts → LLM agents → shared schema → evidence-linked extraction.
Threshold graphic highlighting support from at least 50 abstracts per retained element.
Illustrative abstract-to-table example linking a structured field to supporting text.
paper_title: Agentic induction of common data elements and information extraction from sarcoma case report abstracts
paper_authors: Daniel Reichenpfader, Kwaku Appiagyei, Manovah Nadarajah, Ahmed Reda Bahr, Irina Filchenko
